question: What is the primary unit of service in community-centred care?
explanation: Community-centred care shifts the focus from individual pathology to the collective well-being of the population as the primary unit of service. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why is community-centred care emphasized in Nigerian nursing education?

options.B: To align with national health policies championing primary health care
options.D: To focus solely on curative medicine

explanation: Nursing education emphasizes this framework to align with national health policies that champion primary health care as the bedrock for universal health coverage. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h1)

question: Which PHC principle ensures that health services are accessible to all people regardless of socioeconomic status?
explanation: Equitable distribution means health care must be accessible to all individuals regardless of socioeconomic status, prioritizing vulnerable groups. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h2)

question: What does 'appropriate technology' mean in the context of Primary Health Care?

options.A: Using the most expensive diagnostic machines available globally
options.B: Relying entirely on traditional herbal medicine without testing
options.C: Using affordable and manageable tools that the community can maintain

explanation: Appropriate technology refers to scientifically sound, affordable, and adaptable tools that the community can easily manage and maintain. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h2)

question: Which of the following best describes the scope of comprehensive health care?

options.B: Integrating promotion, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation
options.C: Treating only acute infectious diseases in hospitals
options.D: Providing palliative care at the end of life

explanation: Comprehensive health care integrates promotion, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation into a seamless continuum of services. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of rehabilitative services within comprehensive care?

options.A: To administer routine immunizations to infants
options.B: To educate the community on personal hygiene
options.C: To help individuals recover functioning and reintegrate into society

explanation: Rehabilitative services help individuals recovering from injuries or disabilities to regain optimal functioning and reintegrate into society. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h3)

question: When a community health nurse speaks up for marginalized populations to ensure fair resource allocation, what role are they performing?
explanation: Advocacy involves speaking up for vulnerable populations to ensure their health rights are respected and resources are fairly allocated. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h4)

question: Which activity demonstrates the nurse's role as a coordinator in the community?

options.A: Collaborating with local leaders and health workers to streamline service delivery
options.B: Performing major surgical operations in a primary health post
options.C: Prescribing specialized medications without a protocol
options.D: Isolating themselves from traditional community structures

explanation: As coordinators, nurses collaborate with local leaders and other health workers to streamline service delivery and prevent duplicated efforts. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting a community health assessment?

options.A: To penalize community members for poor sanitation
options.B: To systematically collect data to identify and prioritize health needs
options.D: To replace hospital-based data collection entirely

explanation: Community assessment involves systematically collecting and analyzing data to identify and prioritize health needs before planning interventions. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h5)

question: What is a windshield survey primarily used for during a community assessment?

options.A: To perform invasive clinical laboratory tests
options.B: To observe environmental conditions, housing, and water sources firsthand

explanation: A windshield survey allows the nurse to observe environmental conditions, housing, water sources, and community layouts firsthand. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h5)

question: What is the first step toward achieving cultural competence in community nursing?

options.A: Enforcing strict western medical practices without question
options.B: Developing self-awareness of one's own biases and cultural values
options.D: Learning every language spoken in the world

explanation: Cultural competence requires nurses to possess self-awareness of their own biases before trying to understand and respect other cultural beliefs. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h6)

question: How should a culturally competent nurse handle traditional healing practices in the community?

options.A: Ridicule clients who mention using traditional remedies
options.B: Find ways to integrate safe practices while educating clients on evidence-based methods
options.C: Report all traditional healers to the police immediately
options.D: Abandon modern nursing care in favor of traditional methods

explanation: A culturally competent nurse respects clients and integrates safe traditional practices while gently educating them on evidence-based methods. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h6)

question: Why is intersectoral collaboration necessary in community health?

options.A: Health is influenced by multiple factors outside the direct control of the health sector alone
options.B: It allows nurses to avoid clinical duties completely
options.C: It is mandated only for international nongovernmental organizations
options.D: It reduces the need for community involvement

explanation: Intersectoral collaboration is necessary because health is influenced by factors like education, agriculture, and water, requiring multi-sector partnerships. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h7)

question: What is a major benefit of active community participation in health programs?

options.A: It eliminates the need for professional nurses
options.B: It increases the community's commitment and sustainability of the project
options.C: It shifts all financial burdens onto the federal government
options.D: It prevents any future disease outbreaks

explanation: When community members actively participate, their commitment and the overall sustainability of the health project increase significantly. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of evaluating a community health intervention?

options.A: To assign blame for failed projects
options.B: To measure the success of programs against predefined objectives and indicators
options.C: To increase the workload of community health nurses
options.D: To justify stopping all health education activities

explanation: Evaluation involves measuring the success of implemented programs against predefined objectives and indicators established during planning. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h8)

question: How can a nurse ensure the sustainability of a community health program?

options.A: By keeping all project control exclusively in the hands of foreign donors
options.B: By empowering local structures, training volunteers, and integrating into primary health systems
options.C: By hiding project results from community members
options.D: By stopping all evaluations after the first week

explanation: Sustainability is achieved by empowering local community structures, training local volunteers, and integrating programs into existing primary health care systems. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h8)
